title: Revelation 8:1–5
context: The Lamb opens the seventh seal, and heaven is silent for about half an hour. Seven angels receive seven trumpets. Another angel offers incense with the prayers of the saints, then hurls fire from the altar onto the earth.

verses.text: When he opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour.
verses.arminianNotes: The silence may be a pause of awe before judgment or a hush so that the prayers of the saints can be heard.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see reverent silence before God acts.

verses.text: I saw the seven angels who stand before God, and seven trumpets were given to them.
verses.arminianNotes: Seven trumpets recall Jericho and Sinai.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see trumpets as warnings and announcements of judgment.

verses.text: Another angel came and stood over the altar, having a golden censer. Much incense was given to him, that he should add it to the prayers of all the saints on the golden altar which was before the throne.
verses.arminianNotes: Incense is added to the prayers of all the saints. Arminian readers see that prayer matters to God.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see prayer as one of the means God uses to accomplish his purposes.

verses.text: The smoke of the incense, with the prayers of the saints, went up before God out of the angel’s hand.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see that no prayer of the saints is lost.

verses.text: The angel took the censer, and he filled it with the fire of the altar, then threw it on the earth. Thunders, sounds, lightnings, and an earthquake followed.
verses.arminianNotes: Fire from the altar is thrown on the earth. The prayers of chapter 6 are being answered in judgment. Arminian readers see God responding to his people’s cries.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God’s sovereign answer to prayer in the judgments that follow.
